problem.claim: Online calibration of multi-dimensional forecasts over arbitrary convex action sets and norms.

contributions.claim: Reduces calibration error to swap regret using an optimal OLO regularizer, then minimizes swap regret with TreeSwap and Follow-The-Leader.

Provides a setting-independent, efficient algorithm that needs neither an OLO subroutine nor prior knowledge of the optimal regret rate, and outputs distributions over simple averages of past observations.
Proves an exponential-in-1/ε lower bound for ℓ1-calibration on the simplex under the stated dimensionality condition.

stated_novelty.claim: The authors state that their algorithm is identical across all choices of convex set and norm and achieves its guarantee without OLO access or knowledge of ρ.

author_reported_evidence.claim: The authors report that an O(√(ρT)) worst-case regret guarantee implies ε-calibration after T=exp(O(ρ/ε²)) rounds.
For the d-dimensional simplex with ℓ1 norm, the authors report T=exp(O(log d/ε²))=d^{O(1/ε²}), recovering Peng 2025's result.
The authors report that any algorithm guaranteeing εT ℓ1-calibration error on the simplex requires T≥exp(poly(1/ε)) when d≥poly(1/ε), strengthening Peng 2025's lower bound.

narrative_sequence.summary: Defines online calibration for multi-dimensional forecasts over arbitrary convex sets and norms.
Relates calibration to external regret minimization and derives an exponential-round calibration guarantee from an OLO regret rate.
Uses regularizer-based control by swap regret, TreeSwap, and Follow-The-Leader to obtain a uniform efficient algorithm.
Establishes an exponential lower bound in 1/ε for simplex calibration, strengthening prior work.

source_observation.claim: The abstract links a calibration guarantee to a regret guarantee and separately gives a lower bound showing that exponential dependence on inverse accuracy is necessary in the stated simplex regime; it does not establish matching rates.

lessons.interpretation: A compact paper narrative can make the main tradeoff legible by connecting the reduction, instantiated rate, and necessity result.
lessons.application: When presenting a new online-learning method, state the abstract reduction first, instantiate it in a canonical domain, and report a lower bound if available.
lessons.exception: This sequence is unsuitable when no meaningful reduction, canonical instantiation, or comparable lower bound exists.

unknowns: The abstract does not specify the forecast-observation protocol, calibration-error definition beyond the cited ℓ1 case, or constants hidden in asymptotic notation.
The claimed efficiency and guarantee details, including computational complexity and algorithmic assumptions, are not quantified here.

editorial_revisions.before: The abstract links a calibration guarantee to a regret guarantee, then separately states matching-style upper- and lower-bound dependencies on ε.
editorial_revisions.after: The abstract links a calibration guarantee to a regret guarantee and separately gives a lower bound showing that exponential dependence on inverse accuracy is necessary in the stated simplex regime; it does not establish matching rates.
